classification.difficultyReason: Combines factorisation and differentiation, then explains opposite tangent gradients using reflection symmetry.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the tangents at the $x$-intercepts of $f(x)=x^2-4x-45$ have opposite gradients.

answer.short: The $x$-intercepts occur at $x=-5$ and $x=9$. Their tangent gradients are $-14$ and $14$, respectively.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=2x-4\\f(x)&=(x-9)(x+5)\end{align*}$$
At the $x$-intercepts, $(x-9)(x+5)=0$, so $x=9$ or $x=-5$.
$$\begin{align*}f'(9)&=2(9)-4\\f'(9)&=14\\f'(-5)&=2(-5)-4\\f'(-5)&=-14\end{align*}$$
The gradients are equal in magnitude and opposite in sign.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the vertex of the parabola and use symmetry to explain geometrically why the result in part a has occurred.

answer.short: The vertex is $(2,-49)$. The intercepts $(-5,0)$ and $(9,0)$ are reflections across $x=2$, so their tangents are reflections and have equal but opposite gradients.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x_{\text{vertex}}&=\frac{-(-4)}{2(1)}\\x_{\text{vertex}}&=2\\f(2)&=2^2-4(2)-45\\f(2)&=-49\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(2,-49)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=2$. The intercepts at $x=-5$ and $x=9$ are each $7$ units horizontally from this axis. Reflection across $x=2$ maps one tangent onto the other, reversing its slope while preserving its magnitude. Hence the gradients are equal but opposite.
